name: adv_dpo_bad
title: Direct Preference Optimisation with a reference model - eight planted defects
note: Preference training is two copies of one model, one trained and one frozen, and an objective that is a function of the difference between their log-probabilities. The three defects that break the method are all about the reference copy - never switched to eval, never frozen, forwarded with autograd on, and its parameters handed to the optimizer - and no rule models any of them. MLView finds the two loader defects and the missing seed; the MLV2xx family is silent because `dpo_loss()` returns an arithmetic expression, and it declares that silence by name.

expected.defect: the preference-pair training loader does not shuffle
expected.why: preference datasets are usually grouped by prompt source, so the batches stay correlated with whoever wrote the prompt
the per-pair win/lose decisions come back in a different order each run, so a reader cannot line a regression up against the pair that caused it
GPT-2's attention and residual dropout are active throughout, so the reported preference accuracy moves between runs of the same checkpoint

forbidden.why: the F.log_softmax at line 37 feeds torch.gather, not a cross-entropy; there is no CrossEntropyLoss in this project
F.logsigmoid at line 47 is the DPO objective itself, not a binary cross-entropy, and no BCELoss or BCEWithLogitsLoss is constructed anywhere
there is no torch.no_grad() anywhere in this file - that absence is one of the planted defects
DEVICE is chosen by torch.cuda.is_available() at line 27
there is no split call; the train and eval pair sets arrive as parameters
there is no nn.Module subclass defined in this file at all
there is no nn.Module subclass defined in this file at all
no transformers.Trainer is constructed here; the loop is hand-written
the checkpoint is written with policy.save_pretrained() at line 124, which is the HuggingFace API and not a torch.save of a module

unsupported.defect: the training loop never calls optimizer.zero_grad()
unsupported.why: `dpo_loss()` returns `-F.logsigmoid(beta * (policy_margin - reference_margin)).mean()`, an arithmetic expression whose type MLView cannot recover, so `.backward()` never earns the BACKWARD role and the loop is never confirmed. Declared: an `untagged_dataflow` diagnostic names loss.backward() at line 73 and lists MLV201/202/203/205.

unsupported.defect: running_loss is created at line 52, outside the batch loop, and accumulates the live loss tensor across two full GPT-2 forwards per pair
unsupported.why: same cause as the MLV201 row, and declared by the same diagnostic.

unsupported.defect: evaluate_preferences() never calls policy.eval() or reference.eval(), so GPT-2's attention and residual dropout are active for every reported preference accuracy
unsupported.why: the model forward inside the evaluation loop goes through the workspace helper `sequence_logprobs()` rather than being a direct `model(...)` call, so MLV301's eval-region test never sees a forward. This is the `a call through a function this workspace defines` family that ACCURACY section 3 already names as the largest single source of missing ops.

unsupported.defect: evaluate_preferences() is not wrapped in torch.no_grad()
unsupported.why: same cause as the MLV301 row.

unsupported.defect: the reference forward is not wrapped in torch.no_grad() and the reference model is never frozen with requires_grad_(False) or switched to eval
unsupported.why: no rule models a frozen branch inside a training step; the implicit KL term DPO rests on stops existing when the reference drifts.

unsupported.defect: the optimizer owns the reference model's parameters, so the 'frozen' reference is trained alongside the policy
unsupported.why: MLV211 is a later-tier rule that is not built, and it models a model REPLACED after the optimizer was built rather than an optimizer given parameters it must not own.
